title: Handle ESRCH from openByHandleAt in addition to ESTALE in NewPIDHandleFromString
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request!  You are welcome! -->
Addresses an issue when openByHandleAt returns an ESRCH.

I encountered this on podman client `5.8.5` and a podman `5.6.2` machine, running a postgres:17-alpine via testcontainers. The podman log contained 
```
Request Failed(Internal Server Error): retrieving exec session 3d9ee638… from container 0e817257…: getting the PID handle for pid 242727 … openByHandleAt failed: no such process
```
NewPIDHandleFromString handles ESTALE but not ESRCH from openByHandleAt.  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open_by_handle_at.2.html did not list an ESRCH, so I used Claude locally to trace the  issue.

It appears after testcontainers-go started the container, it runs a brief command (see https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go/blob/6e584183e1623fb83a78db902462eb9ee255327b/wait/host_port.go#L314) to check host ports, which took less than the 10ms between `exec` and `exec_died` on the machine's journal.

The `exec inspect`'s  `open_by_handle_at` ran at this time, and on my machine's kernel version (6.15.10-200.fc42) [pidfs_export_open](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.15.10/source/fs/pidfs.c#L804) returns ESRCH when [pidfs_pid_valid](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.15.10/source/fs/pidfs.c#L766) returns false because it was in the process of being reaped.

comments.body:
I will reproduce what claude discovered in my own words here
**Podman (main)** (HTTP request -> syscall)
1. GET /v1.41/exec/{id}/json -> compat.ExecInspectHandler (pkg/api/server/register_exec.go:179).
2. ExecInspectHandler -> sessionCtr.ExecSession(sessionID) (pkg/api/handlers/compat/exec.go:130-132)
3. Container.ExecSession -> execSessionNoCopy (libpod/container.go:1004).
4. execSessionNoCopy -> c.ociRuntime.ExecUpdateStatus (libpod/container.go:989)
5. ExecUpdateStatus -> pidhandle.NewPIDHandleFromString (libpod/oci_conmon_exec_common.go:277).
6. NewPIDHandleFromString -> openByHandleAt (unix.OpenByHandleAt) (pkg/pidhandle/pidhandle_linux.go:128).

**Kernel (v6.15.10)** (syscall -> pidfs_export_open)
7. SYSCALL_DEFINE3 -> do_handle_open (fs/fhandle.c:434).
8. do_handle_open (fs/fhandle.c:443)-> handle_to_path (fs/fhandle.c:403):
  - eops->permission passes
  - do_handle_to_path -> exportfs_decode_fh_raw -> fh_to_dentry -> pidfs_fh_to_dentry (fs/pidfs.c:712). At this point the theory is the pid was still in pidfs's table, it returns a dentry not NULL (NULL would result in ESTALE)
9. Back in do_handle_open -> eops->open (fs/fhandle.c:413) -> pidfs_export_open (fs/pidfs.c:804)
10. pidfs_export_open (fs/pidfs.c:805) -> pidfs_pid_valid. The process unlinked from its PID (in theory) and returns false
11. do_handle_open returns error, reported eventually as ESRCH
I am really grateful for the fast and detailed review. I've updated with the requested changes and amended the commit.
